drills.label: Cold open
drills.question_line: SAM: A legal research agent runs on Claude Opus five.
drills.answer_line: SAM: A. Retention is the default on keep-all models
drills.scenario: Research agent, context growing from old thinking
drills.stem: A research agent on Claude Opus 5 sees input tokens grow far faster than its retrieved documents. Every earlier assistant turn's thinking blocks are still in each request. What is going on, and what should the team do?

options.A: Documented default for Opus 5; use thinking block clearing via context editing to reclaim space
options.B: The API always strips old thinking, so the client is duplicating blocks; fix the serialiser
options.C: Turn thinking off for the rest of the conversation
options.D: A client bug; delete every thinking block older than two turns before each request

drills.why: Opus 5 keeps all prior thinking, counted as input. B describes last-turn-only models. C loses reasoning and fails at xhigh and max. D hand-edits the prefix.

drills.label: Drill
drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. A retailer's returns assistant on Fable five point one
drills.answer_line: SAM: Right. B lengthens the life of a prefix that never matches.
drills.scenario: Returns assistant, cache misses and binding errors
drills.stem: A returns assistant on Fable 5.1 rebuilds its system prompt every call: role, returns policy, then today's order details. Cache hits are near zero and follow-ups fail with a binding error. What fixes both?

options.A: Fixed system prompt for role and policy; each order's details in the user turn
options.B: Set a one-hour cache time to live
options.C: Strip all earlier thinking blocks before each request
options.D: Move everything into the first user message, empty system prompt

drills.why: A stable prefix caches and stops invalidating thinking blocks. B cannot make a changing prefix match. C leaves the cache cold. D still changes the first thing sent.

drills.label: Drill
drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. Choose two. A clinic-scheduling vendor has Z D R
drills.answer_line: ALEX: A and C. B is the HIPAA blocking rule
drills.scenario: Clinic-scheduling vendor, ZDR claim to auditors
drills.stem: A vendor with ZDR plans to tell auditors Anthropic keeps nothing. They use the Messages API, the Files API for referral letters, and nightly batches. Which two statements correct the plan?

options.A: Files and batch jobs fall outside ZDR and follow their own retention
options.B: The API rejects ineligible features under ZDR, so the plan is safe
options.C: Content flagged by trust and safety may still be kept for up to two years
options.D: ZDR switches on by default for paid organisations
options.E: A new organisation under the same account inherits ZDR

drills.why: ZDR covers eligible features only and does not block the rest; blocking is HIPAA behaviour. It is requested through sales and enabled per organisation.

drills.label: Drill
drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. An insurer's claims-review agent
drills.answer_line: SAM: B. C may save money, but it dodges
drills.stem: A claims-review agent reasons through one claim file in a single dependent chain, well inside one context window. The team wants a cheaper design. What does the guidance suggest first?

options.A: A frontier planner with three cheaper workers
options.B: Keep one model and sweep effort for the cheapest level that holds quality
options.C: Move to the Batch API and change nothing else
options.D: An advisor pattern with the cheapest model as executor

drills.why: For one dependent chain in one context, the single model at lower effort came out ahead. Batch dodges the question; A and D add a model the work does not justify.

drills.label: Drill
drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. Choose two. An accounts-payable agent
drills.answer_line: SAM: Correct. Ask who controls the text.
drills.stem: An accounts-payable agent reads supplier invoices and emails. Which two belong in the indirect-injection section of its threat model?

options.A: A supplier email hides text telling the agent to change bank details on file
options.B: A user role-plays as an auditor over several turns to get past a refusal
options.C: The developer's formatting rules, placed inside the tool result, are ignored as possibly injected
options.D: One account trips the same content filter all week and is throttled

drills.why: Indirect: a trusted user, third-party content. Claude treats tool-result content as untrusted, so your own instructions there may be ignored. B and D are the user as adversary.

drills.question_line: SAM: Before the last word, pause and name the five gaps
drills.answer_line: ALEX: Thinking retention by model. Append-only history on Fable.
drills.prompt: Name the five gaps this episode closed without looking back.
drills.answer: Thinking retention by model; append-only history on Fable 5.1; the edges of ZDR; effort before orchestration; instructions out of tool results.

In this episode: Which models keep earlier thinking, and how to reclaim the space
Why rebuilding the system prompt breaks a Fable 5.1 conversation
What zero data retention does and does not cover
Why an effort sweep comes before an orchestrator
Why your own instructions stay out of tool results
Choose-two: read every option to the last word
Thinking blocks by model: Keep all prior turns: Opus 4.5+, Sonnet 4.6+, Haiku 5.5, Fable and Mythos
Last turn only: earlier Opus and Sonnet, Haiku up to 4.5; API strips old blocks
Retained thinking counts as input like any other history
Reclaim space with thinking block clearing (context editing); cache restarts there
In a tool-use turn, pass thinking back complete and unmodified
Opus 5 at xhigh or max: thinking cannot be disabled (400)
Append-only history on Fable: Each thinking block is bound to the system prompt, tools and earlier messages
Change any of them: 400, 'bound to a different conversation'
Causes: rebuilt system prompt or tools, edited turns, injected then deleted reminders
Same root cause as a cache that never hits
Fix: stable system prompt; per-request content in the user turn
New instructions: mid-conversation system message; trim with context editing or compaction
What zero data retention covers: Requested through sales, enabled per organisation; new orgs need it separately
Eligible features only: Files API kept until deleted or expired; Batch 29 days
Code execution, MCP connector, Managed Agents also outside it
Under ZDR the API does not block ineligible features; HIPAA-ready does (400)
Flagged by trust and safety: kept up to 2 years; legal holds apply
Fable and Mythos need 30-day retention: not under ZDR unless authorised
Effort before orchestration: Tune one model before adding a second
Sweep 2 or 3 effort levels on your own traffic, each in its own session
Plot score against spend: the baseline any pairing must beat
Orchestrator pays only for a long cost tail or work beyond one context
One dependent chain in one context: single model at lower effort wins
Advisor helps only if the executor consults it and lacks the capability
Instructions in tool results: Indirect injection: the user is trusted, third-party content is not
Deliver untrusted content in tool results, with its source named
System prompt: tool content is data and never overrides the user
JSON-encode untrusted strings; screen tool output; least privilege
Your own instructions in a tool result may be ignored or flagged
Send them in the next user turn or a mid-conversation system message
Five to remember: Newer models keep all prior thinking; clear it with thinking block clearing
Fable 5.1 history is append-only: rebuilt system prompt = binding error + cold cache
ZDR: per organisation, eligible features only, not enforced, flagged content kept
Sweep effort on one model before splitting the work
Your instructions go in the user turn, never inside a tool result
Recap: the exam tells: Context grows from old thinking → keep-all default, thinking block clearing
'Bound to a different conversation' or no cache hits → system prompt rebuilt per request
ZDR covers everything, blocks features, or is automatic → wrong
One dependent chain in one context → single model, effort sweep; batch is a dodge
Developer instruction inside a tool result → expect it ignored
Cold open: the swelling context: Input grows faster than retrieved documents
Old thinking blocks in every request
